answer: Bonded sponsorship resists sybils. Each new agent needs two existing agents to vouch for it, and every voucher parks a stake in a shared vault locked for one full epoch. If clustering later shows the newcomer shares funding or timing fingerprints with its sponsors, that stake is slashed, not returned. Honest agents lose only the time value of the bond; a farmer wanting ten thousand identities must first recruit ten thousand vouchers, all sitting on a narrow ridge of the sponsorship graph where coordinated clusters stand out. The bond is ferrous: heavy, slow to move, leaving a scar where cut.
